name: Stereo Pseudo 3D Rendering via Image Stacks
aliases: Pseudo Stereo Pair Generation, Stereo Pseudo 3D, Web-based Stereo Pseudo 3D
text:
# Stereo Pseudo 3D Rendering via Image Stacks Also called: Pseudo Stereo Pair Generation, Stereo Pseudo 3D, Web-based Stereo Pseudo 3D ## Overview This method generates a stereo pair of images from a pre-existing 2D image stack to simulate binocular parallax and volumetric depth perception using standard web technologies [S1]. It solves the problem of visualizing scientific volumetric data in a browser without specialized hardware or client-side rendering engines [S1]. It is distinguished from full [ray-casting volume rendering](#3462-volumetric-raycasting.md) by relying on image overlay and CSS positioning rather than per-pixel shading, and from single-slice viewers like BrainMaps.org by allowing simultaneous visibility of multiple depth layers [S1]. ## How it works **Inputs and Outputs** * **Input:** A stack of $N$ 2D images (e.g., PNG slices) representing cross-sections of a volume [S1]. * **Output:** Two HTML DOM trees (stacks) containing positioned `` elements that produce a 3D effect when viewed with stereo merging [S1]. **Data Structures** The implementation relies on the HTML Document Object Model (DOM) [S1]. * **Containers:** Two `
` elements with `position: absolute` CSS styling [S1]. One serves as the base stack (`imgstacks`), the other as the offset stack (`imgoffsets`) [S1]. * **Image Elements:** `` nodes created dynamically [S1]. Each has `position: absolute`, and explicit `top`, `left`, `width`, and `height` style properties [S1]. * **Preprocessing:** Input images must have alpha channels added, with background pixels set to transparent to allow proper overlay blending [S1]. **Numbered Steps** 1. **Preprocess Images:** Convert input slices to PNG format with transparent backgrounds [S1]. Generate a single semi-opaque white image (e.g., 180x180 pixels, 10% opacity) to be reused for [distance attenuation](#18491-fragment-attenuation-models.md) [S1]. 2. **Initialize DOM:** Create two absolute-positioned `
` containers in the HTML structure: one for the base stack and one for the offset stack [S1]. 3. **Generate Base Stack:** Iterate through the image stack from $i = 0$ to $N-1$ [S1]. For each data slice $i$: create an `` element, set `src` to the data slice, set `position` to `absolute`, and set `top` and `left` to the base coordinates (e.g., 0,0 relative to container) [S1]. Append to the base stack container [S1]. Insert the semi-opaque white image between every pair of data slices to simulate distance attenuation (aerial perspective) [S1]. 4. **Generate Offset Stack:** Iterate through the image stack from $i = 0$ to $N-1$ [S1]. For each data slice $i$: create an `` element, set `src` to the data slice, set `position` to `absolute`, calculate horizontal position: $x_i = x_{i-1} + \Delta x$, where for the first slice $x_0$ is the base left position, set `left` to $x_i$, keep `top` identical to the base stack, and append to the offset stack container [S1]. Insert the semi-opaque white image between every pair of data slices in the offset stack as well [S1]. 5. **Display:** Load both stacks into the browser [S1]. The combined result is viewed with stereo merging to perceive the 3D effect [S1]. **Formulas** * Horizontal offset accumulation: $x_i = x_{i-1} + \Delta x$ for $i > 0$, with $x_0 = x_{\text{base}}$ [S1]. * Distance attenuation: achieved by interleaving a semi-opaque layer with opacity $\alpha$ between data slices [S1]. **Parameters** * **Opacity of interleaving layer ($\alpha$):** Typically 10% (0.1) for the semi-opaque white image [S1]. * **Horizontal offset per slice ($\Delta x$):** Typically 1 pixel relative to the previous slice's position [S1]. * **Eye separation:** Approximately 6 cm, used to calculate horizontal disparities for stereoscopic depth perception [S1]. * **Image Resolution:** Example usage subsampled to 180x180 pixels from 512x512 source [S1]. **Edge Cases and Pitfalls** * **Pseudo-Accuracy:** Fixed linear offsetting produces "pseudo" accurate stereo pairs, not fully accurate geometric projections [S1]. Nonlinear offsetting based on a depth function can improve accuracy but is not implemented in the basic method [S1]. * **Viewpoint Rigidity:** The viewpoint is predetermined by the image stack organization [S1]. Interactive viewpoint changes ([rotation](#19376-rotation.md), zoom) are not supported on the fly [S1]. * **Viewer Strain:** Stereo merging requires the user to perform cross-viewing or parallel viewing, which can cause eye strain [S1]. Optical aids (mirrors/prisms) may be required [S1]. * **Performance Scaling:** Memory and load time scale linearly with the number of images [S1]. **Pseudocode** > **Unverified code.** The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. ```python class DOMElement: def __init__(self, tag, attrs=None): self.tag = tag self.attrs = attrs or {} self.children = [] def append(self, child): self.children.append(child) def generate_stereo_pseudo_3d(image_stack, num_slices, offset_per_slice=1, opacity=0.1): """ Generates DOM structures for stereo pseudo 3D rendering. image_stack: List of image data/paths. num_slices: Number of data slices N. offset_per_slice: Horizontal pixel shift per slice depth. opacity: Opacity of the interleaving attenuation layer. """ # 1. Preprocessing assumed done: images are transparent PNGs. # Generate a single semi-opaque white image for attenuation. attenuation_image = {"src": "attenuation_10pct.png", "opacity": opacity} # 2. Initialize DOM containers base_container = DOMElement("div", {"id": "imgstacks", "position": "absolute"}) offset_container = DOMElement("div", {"id": "imgoffsets", "position": "absolute"}) content_container = DOMElement("div", {"id": "imgcontent", "position": "absolute"}) content_container.append(base_container) content_container.append(offset_container) # 3. Build Base Stack current_top = 0 current_left = 0 for i in range(num_slices): # Add data slice img_elem = DOMElement("img", {"src": image_stack[i], "position": "absolute", "top": str(current_top) + "px", "left": str(current_left) + "px"}) base_container.append(img_elem) # Add attenuation layer between slices (except after the last one) if i < num_slices - 1: att_img = DOMElement("img", {"src": attenuation_image["src"], "position": "absolute", "top": str(current_top) + "px", "left": str(current_left) + "px"}) base_container.append(att_img) # 4. Build Offset Stack offset_top = 0 offset_left = 0 for i in range(num_slices): # Add data slice with cumulative horizontal offset current_offset_x = offset_left + i * offset_per_slice img_elem = DOMElement("img", {"src": image_stack[i], "position": "absolute", "top": str(offset_top) + "px", "left": str(current_offset_x) + "px"}) offset_container.append(img_elem) # Add attenuation layer if i < num_slices - 1: att_img = DOMElement("img", {"src": attenuation_image["src"], "position": "absolute", "top": str(offset_top) + "px", "left": str(current_offset_x) + "px"}) offset_container.append(att_img) return content_container ``` ## Operating characteristics * **Time Complexity:** Linear $O(N)$ with respect to the number of images $N$ for loading and DOM construction [S1]. * **Memory Complexity:** Linear $O(N)$, as each image is stored in the browser cache and DOM [S1]. * **Measured Performance:** On a 1.7 GHz PC with 1GB RAM, displaying 50 overlayed images took approximately 3 seconds after download [S1]. Load time and memory usage scaled linearly for 15, 30, and 50 images (95kB–126kB each) on Firefox 2.0 and IE 7.0 [S1]. * **Strengths:** Requires no specialized software, hardware, or client-side computation; works in standard web browsers with CSS/JS support [S1]. Allows viewing multiple stacked images simultaneously to perceive volumetric structures [S1]. * **Limitations:** No interactive viewpoint changes; stereo accuracy is approximate; requires user ability to merge stereo images; potential eye strain [S1]. * **When to Use:** Web-based display of static scientific volumetric data where interactive 3D rendering is not feasible or necessary [S1]. * **When Not to Use:** When interactive viewpoint changes or high-precision geometric stereo are required [S1]. ## Background The method was developed by D. C.-Y. Eng and Y. Choe and presented at the Pacific Graphics 2008 conference [S1]. It was applied to visualize 50 slices of mouse spinal cord scans from the KESM dataset, where blood vessels were stained with India ink [S1]. The approach contrasts with BrainMaps.org, which displays one slide at a time, and other web-based 3D approaches that require specialized software or hardware [S1]. ## Sources [S1] Stereo Pseudo 3D Rendering for Web-based Display of Scientific Volumetric Data, https://doi.org/10.2312/vg/vg-pbg08/073-080, fetched 2026-10-26
